text: In the context of the instrumental cause (nimitta), the non-instrumental cause (naimittika), and the occasion (prasaṅga), the instrumental cause is dharma and so on, while the non-instrumental cause is upward movement and so on; these will be explained earlier. The occasion (prasaṅga) is the attachment (prasaṅgya) of the primordial nature (prakṛti) to the Supreme Lord (pradhāna) through the union of its potency (vibhūtvayoga), just as a king, by virtue of his sovereignty in his own kingdom, does whatever he wishes. Similarly, through the union of its potency in all things, the primordial nature, by way of the occasion, subsists as the instrumental and non-instrumental causes, and it establishes the distinct arrangement of the body-bearers (dehadhāraṇa) and the linga.
